name: Nueva Esparta · Margarita
summary: A Spanish pearl island becomes a stronghold of Venezuelan independence.
notes: Margarita is the historical proxy for modern Nueva Esparta, which also includes Coche and Cubagua. These islands are not individually tracked. The 1810–1817 struggle involved overlapping royalist and republican control; the chart explicitly uses a contested interval.

events.title: Spain claims Margarita
events.detail: Columbus’s voyage reached the island; pearl extraction drove subsequent colonial interest.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: A Spanish governorship
events.detail: Margarita was organized as a Spanish provincial governorship.

events.title: Margarita joins the revolutionary movement
events.detail: A local junta joined the independence movement; royalist and republican power repeatedly contested the island.

events.title: Venezuelan independence declared
events.detail: Margarita was among the provinces declaring independence; war continued.

events.title: Royalist government returns
events.detail: The collapse of the First Republic brought a royalist governor; revolutionary resistance persisted.

events.title: Republicans recover the initiative
events.detail: An uprising freed Arismendi and put revolutionary forces back in command.

events.title: Morillo’s expedition
events.detail: A Spanish expedition imposed a new royalist presence, followed by renewed resistance.

events.title: Spanish forces leave Margarita
events.detail: Island resistance defeated Morillo’s final campaign; Spain evacuated.

events.title: Part of the Republic of Colombia
events.detail: The republican territories were united in the state now called Gran Colombia.

events.title: Venezuela separates from Gran Colombia
events.detail: Margarita remained with the new Venezuelan republic.
